BAMOR

Project brief

BAMOR explores the potential of applying bamboo and other naturally elastic materials to responsive soft robotic architecture. Unlike conventional temporary performance installations that primarily rely on industrial materials and static structures, the project utilizes the inherent flexibility of bamboo to construct a lightweight, deployable bamboo–textile structure that is easy to transport and assemble, and applies it to a small-scale performance and viewing space. The system enhances the relationship between people and space through two modes of interaction: in everyday use, the installation recognizes users’ postures and positions in real time and adaptively adjusts its spatial form to accommodate different needs for rest and activity; in performance settings, the installation captures the tempo and beats of music in real time, driving the structural blades to produce rhythmic dynamic responses, allowing the space itself to participate in the performance and enhancing the immersive experience of performers and audiences. BAMOR thus combines natural materials, lightweight deployable structures, and real-time interaction, while reducing the environmental impact of temporary installations through the renewable and biodegradable material life cycle of bamboo, exploring a more sustainable dynamic architectural environment with sensing and responsive capabilities.
